title: applied-ml quant eval scratchpad
content:
Quick scratchpad for quantization + prompt eval runs (personal notes)

Context:
- Trying 4-bit/8-bit quantization profiles on chat-generation workloads (gpt-like transformer, 6B) to get cost/latency wins while keeping quality within acceptable regressions.
- Baseline: fp16 (current serving config). Runs done on dev-cluster (A100s) and small local dev box (rtx6000).
- Primary metrics: p50/p95 token latency, generation token/sec, win rate on human eval set, avg logprob / perplexity on eval set, and alignment with eval prompts.

Experiments run (notes):
- exp-20260226-q4k-lite: 4-bit symmetric, GPTQ-ish flow (hf-quant, backend=open-source), batch_size=1 for latency, batch_size=8 for throughput tests.
  - p50 token latency: 18ms (vs baseline 12ms) -> regression but cost reduced ~2.5x per-token.
  - p95 token latency: 65ms (vs baseline 40ms) -> noticeable tail latency increase.
  - Quality quick check: BLEU/ROUGE not great metric here; used 100-shot pairwise human-ish comparisons on 50 prompts: 82% preference for baseline, 18% for q4 (mostly shorter outputs collapse).
  - Notes: prefix KV cache behaves weirdly on cold-start with q4 kernel; need to confirm cache compatibility.

- exp-20260227-q8-mixed: 8-bit asymmetric + weight-only quantization (per-channel), backend=custom-kernel (serving-runtime branch: pr-1234), batch=1
  - p50 token latency: 14ms; p95: 45ms. Better than q4 for tail.
  - Quality: near-indistinguishable on instruction-following tasks; slight hallucination increase on abstractive QA (small sample).
  - Throughput (batch=8): 540 tokens/sec vs baseline 800 tokens/sec on same hw.

Prompt sets used (quick):
- prompt-set-A: customer-facing chat style (greeting + ask + context) x 200 examples
- prompt-set-B: summarization of long docs (avg 800 tokens) x 50 examples
- prompt-set-C: code generation snippets (short) x 100 examples
- Observed q4 failing more on prompt-set-B (long context -> repeated token collapse)

Quant configs to test next (todo):
- q4 + KV-cache-fix; rerun cold-start tails (owner: Evan)
- per-channel q4 (not global) -> test on small model first
- 4/8 hybrid: first N layers 8-bit, last layers 4-bit (hypothesis: preserve conditioning fidelity)
- test with int8 quant backend (onnxruntime / triton) vs our custom kernels (latency tradeoffs)

Quick commands I ran (notes to self):
- python run_eval.py --model /models/gpt-6b --quant q4_sym --backend hf-quant --batch 1 --prompts data/prompt-set-A.json 
- python run_eval.py --model /models/gpt-6b --quant q8_pc --backend custom --batch 8 --prompts data/prompt-set-B.json
- docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/work redwood/serving-runtime:pr-1234 /bin/bash -c "./bench_tokens.sh --model /work/models/gpt-6b --workers 4"

Preliminary takeaways:
- q4 gives cost wins but tail latency and some quality regressions are non-trivial for long-context tasks. Might be acceptable for short chat snippets or high-temperature generation where diversity is desired.
- q8 (per-channel) seems like a reasonable middle ground with smaller quality hit and acceptable latency.
- Need to instrument more: token-level divergence plot (first 64 tokens), and per-prompt failure modes (where hallucinations increase).

Open questions / things to debug:
- Why does q4 increase p95 so much on cold starts? hypothesis: kernel fallback + cache warming + fragmentation. Check GPU memory fragmentation and async memcpy patterns. -> link to perf traces in slack thread.
- KV-cache invariants: are we accidentally invalidating cache due to quant rounding on key projection? Add unit test to validate cache identicalness between fp16 and quantized (same seeds) for first 32 steps.
- Eval harness: need better automatic metrics for chat quality (win-rate from automatic preference model?). Maya working on pairwise automatic scoring model — loop in.

TODO (short):
- [ ] Add unit test for KV cache equality (Evan)
- [ ] Run per-layer hybrid quant experiment (Ravi)
- [ ] Push microbench kernel profiling (serving-runtime/pr-1234) and capture traces (perf + nvprof) (Evan)
- [ ] Collate human eval results into confluence page (Maya)

Next steps (next week):
1) run q4 + cache-invariant test; collect p50/p95 + token divergence plots (Evan)
2) run hybrid layer quant (first 6 layers 8-bit, last 18 layers 4-bit) on small model and compare quality/latency (Ravi)
3) prototype automatic preference scoring on 500 prompt pairs (Maya)

Notes to self / random thoughts:
- Maybe a rolling fallback policy: try q4 for tail-tolerant endpoints, auto-fallback to q8 for prompts longer than X tokens or when early tokens have low logprob. Could be integrated into smart routing.
- Keep an eye on ppl/perplexity for long-doc summarization — sometimes lower ppl with quant but worse human preference (weird).
